name: Mood and Stress
subtitle: Stress, Anxiety and Mood
instructions: Think about the past week specifically. For each statement, rate how often it applied to you during that time. Use 1 (Rarely or not at all) to 4 (Most of the time).

questions.text: Even tasks that feel well within your ability have required noticeably more effort than usual to start or finish.
You have noticed your mouth going dry in situations that shouldn't really be stressful, like a routine meeting, a phone call, or just waiting for something.
Things that would normally make you feel something, a good meal, a message from a friend, a piece of music you like, just haven't been landing the way they usually do.
Your breathing has felt slightly off at certain moments, shorter or faster than the situation seems to call for.
There has been a kind of inertia to the week, a gap between knowing what you should do and actually being able to get moving on it.
Small things, a slow connection, someone running a few minutes late, a minor inconvenience, have set you off more than they normally would.
There has been a physical unsteadiness at times, a slight tremor or a feeling that your legs are less solid than usual.
Even when the day is over and nothing is demanding your attention, switching off has felt harder than it should be.
Things coming up that would normally give you something to look forward to, plans with people, upcoming events, haven't been generating much genuine anticipation.
You have found yourself in situations that seemed fine on paper but that you were quietly relieved to get out of, like a social event or a meeting.
You have felt like you are running on reserves this week, doing what needs to be done but aware that it is costing more than it usually does.
When you try to picture the near future, next week or next month, there is not much there that feels genuinely worth waiting for.
There has been a restlessness, a sense of being just slightly on edge, sitting below the surface for most of the day.
At certain points, a wave of something close to panic has come over you, a sudden sense that things are about to go badly.
There has been a flatness to the week, a heaviness that is hard to name but that has made everything feel a bit more effortful than usual.
Getting to a point in the evening where your mind genuinely quiets down has been harder than it normally is.
In certain situations, a presentation or a gathering, you have been quietly preoccupied with the idea of losing composure in front of others.
At points during the week, it has been difficult to see what the point of things is, or what you are actually working toward.
Interruptions, a noise, a question, someone needing something while you are mid task, have been harder to absorb without irritation.
Your hands or another part of your body have had a slight trembling quality at moments when you are under any kind of pressure.
The week has felt emotionally flat overall, not necessarily bad, but with very little in the way of genuine positive feeling.
You have found it hard to wind down after something demanding, your body or mind stays activated even when the situation is over.
You have felt afraid without being able to point to a clear or reasonable cause for it.
There have been moments where life has felt meaningless, not catastrophic, but empty in a way that is hard to shake.
You have been more reactive than usual, finding that things get under your skin faster and more intensely than they normally would.
You have noticed that your heart has been racing or pounding at moments that don't obviously call for it, sitting quietly, preparing for something routine.
You have noticed that you don't feel much enthusiasm about anything this week, even things you would normally look forward to.
You have felt easily agitated this week. Things that usually wash over you have been catching and holding in a way they don't normally.
There have been moments where you felt genuinely afraid that something terrible was about to happen, without anything in the situation that would fully account for it.
You have felt like you don't have much worth as a person this week, a quiet but persistent sense that you are falling short in some fundamental way.
You have been less patient this week. The usual tolerance you have for friction or delay has been thinner than normal.
You have been aware of your own swallowing more than usual, a kind of self-consciousness about something as ordinary as that.
You have found it hard to feel genuinely good about anything you have done this week, even things that went well.
You have found it hard to relax even in downtime, your mind or body still carrying tension from the day.
There have been moments where you felt like you might faint or lose your footing, a sudden physical instability without a clear cause.
You have felt like life holds very little interest or reward for you this week, that things are going through the motions rather than feeling alive.
You have felt on edge in a way that is difficult to account for, as though something is building without a specific reason behind it.
There have been moments where you were aware of your pulse in places you don't normally notice it, your throat, your temples, your chest.
There have been moments this week where you felt close to tears without a clear trigger, a general heaviness that surfaces unprompted.
You have found it hard to tolerate anything that delays or disrupts your plans, even minor changes have felt more frustrating than they should.
You have felt genuinely scared at certain points this week without being able to fully explain what you were scared of.
You have found it difficult to feel any genuine interest or investment in the things in front of you this week, a flatness that makes even ordinary tasks feel pointless.
